_README: The single rules file for the coloradostartups.org content gate.
Read by 04_tools/cs_site_lint.py, which every call site shells out to (the
PostToolUse content guard, .githooks/pre-commit and pre-push, and CI), and by
04_tools/contract_test.py, which asserts this file still agrees with the
settings file, the hooks, the gate table in .claude/rules/site-gates.md and the LinkedIn sister gate.
Precedence: ~/.claude/rules/writing-and-gates.md and compute.md win
over this file. Remedy: when they disagree, fix this file in the same session
and rerun python3 04_tools/contract_test.py.
Shared rules (see shared_from) must keep the same id, regex, severity,
case_sensitive and after_expiry as the LinkedIn file. Change both together;
contract_test.py C2 fails when they drift.
A rule's severity_built, when set, replaces its severity in --built mode only
(site/dist). It is the site's own escalation, like the LinkedIn file's
severity_buffer, so C2 does not compare it. Three more site-only fields:
built_types limits a rule in --built mode to those file types; built_skip_tags
names HTML tags whose text that rule alone skips; exempt_match lets through a
match it covers whole, so a shared regex stays the LinkedIn file's.
Private rules (the avoid list) live in cs_site_rules.private.json, which never
leaves the private archive repo. cs_site_lint.py merges it when present
(CS_SITE_PRIVATE_RULES names another path) and runs on these public rules
alone, with a note, when it is absent. Open-source plan, #552.
Every rule carries at least one 'hit' and one 'miss' sample.
cs_site_lint.py --self-test runs every sample, so a regex that stops matching
its own example fails the self-test.
Block on the certain, warn on the likely. FAIL is for literal names and phrases
with one meaning. Anything a reader must judge is WARN.
Generic prose rules come from 04_tools/voice_lint.py, vendored verbatim from
SoulCraft-Org/git-crafter tools/voice_lint.py (its first lines name the commit;
never edited here). 'rules' is passed to voice_lint's own rules loader, so the severity
overrides, attribution cues and figure nouns go through voice_lint.
The term rules below do NOT go through voice_lint: it replaces URLs with a
placeholder and compiles every pattern case-insensitive, so coloradoai.us inside
a link and the case_sensitive rules would misfire. cs_site_lint.py runs them on
the raw extracted text instead, the same split the LinkedIn gate uses.

_severity_notes.em-dash: FAIL: a literal character test (house rule: no em dashes).
_severity_notes.spaced-en-dash: FAIL: the house rule treats a spaced en dash as an em dash.
_severity_notes.unattributed-figure: WARN: voice_lint's own docstring calls it a heuristic.
_severity_notes.hedge-word: WARN: heuristic; 'rather' and 'quite' have honest uses.
_severity_notes.sentence-length: WARN: heuristic; lists and addresses run long.

_README: Paths are relative to the repository root. 'content' is what the source lint
covers: data files and art prompts. A file outside 'content', or matching
'never', is skipped silently, so code, docs and these tools never trip the
gate. 'built' is the --built mode: the generated HTML, text and JSON files,
which catches what templates and public files add after the data files pass
(robots.txt, llms.txt, feed.json, data/resources.json). The lint reads the
file types these globs name; a type it has no extractor for is a rules error.
How prose is pulled out of each file type before any rule runs.
YAML and Markdown front matter: only string values are linted. Values whose
owning key is in skip_keys are skipped, unless a rule sets
scan_skipped_keys (link and path rules, because a coloradoai.us URL in a
url field is still a link). A rule with 'fields' runs only on values of
those keys. HTML: visible text only; html_skip_tags are never read.
Built text: every line. Built JSON: string values only, each owned by its
key as in YAML (a list item by the key that holds the list), so skip_keys
apply. A built JSON file that does not parse is 'could not check' (exit 3).
Rules copied from the LinkedIn sister gate. Same organization, same avoid list.
contract_test.py C2 compares id, regex, severity, case_sensitive and
after_expiry for every id below when the file exists, and prints SKIP when it
does not (CI cannot see it). Windows are not compared: this file follows
The private overlay adds its own shared_ids; C2 compares both lists.
LinkedIn LOG decision 39 for coloradoai-link, which the LinkedIn file has not
picked up yet.
The LinkedIn file's path is private: it sits in the overlay as linkedin_rules_path.

rules.message: third-party franchise name; the Hall's theme stays original and never borrows a name from Tolkien, Warcraft or Zelda
rules.source: Site brief for the Hall theme (orchestrator Wave 0 gate spec, 2026-10-08). 'paths' is an exempt-list analogue: docs that explain the ban may name these, content may not. contract_test.py C3 pins the list. Extended to Nintendo and Zelda names and more Tolkien and Warcraft names on 2026-11-02 (decision 90).
rules._note: Case-insensitive for names with one meaning. Case-sensitive for 'Great Forge', 'Lonely Mountain' and 'Middle Earth', so 'a great forge' passes. 'Blizzard' alone is a Colorado weather word; a bare match would block every storm report, so only 'Blizzard Entertainment' and 'Blizzard Games' block. 'Warcraft' covers 'World of Warcraft'. Bare 'Zelda' and 'Link' stay out: both are real first names or common words, and the gate blocks only on the certain, so the series' full title blocks instead. 'Ocarina' alone is an instrument, so only 'Ocarina of Time' blocks. 'Death Mountain', 'Breath of the Wild' and 'Tears of the Kingdom' are case-sensitive like 'Great Forge'. 'Misty Mountains' is case-sensitive too, so 'misty mountains at dawn' passes; 'Mount Doom' and 'Mt. Doom' block in any case. Gimli and Thorin stay out: Tolkien took both from Norse myth, and Gimli is also a town in Manitoba. Bare 'Majora' (a real given name) and 'Mithril' (Mithril Capital, a real VC firm) stay out; only 'Majora's Mask' blocks.

not_lintable.rule: Content made with AI help says so where the site's disclosure policy requires it.
not_lintable.enforced_by: Human review of the pull request. A text lint cannot tell whether AI helped write a page, and the absence of a disclosure line is not a string to match. The orchestrator names the disclosure surface (component or page) in .claude/rules/ai-disclosure.md.
